sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +24 days over 5 years while revenue compounded -3.5%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.

Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +13.3 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved +0 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 6.9 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 6.9 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 14.0% with ROE of 9.9% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 518 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 3 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 48 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 3 hard red flags and 4 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 48/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
